name: The Isley Brothers
hook: A gospel trio that outlasted six musical eras, briefly employed a young Jimi Hendrix, and left behind two of the most sampled records in hip-hop.
blurb: O'Kelly, Rudolph and Ronald Isley began singing gospel together in Cincinnati in 1954 and moved through doo-wop, rock and roll, soul and funk over six decades, briefly employing a young guitarist named Jimi Hendrix in their backing band in the mid-1960s. They started their own label, T-Neck Records. In the early 1970s they added the younger brothers Ernie and Marvin and their brother-in-law Chris Jasper as an in-house rock and funk band, and their willingness to keep changing kept them selling in every era. Their 1969 hit 'It's Your Thing' and 1975's 'Fight the Power' became two of the most sampled records in hip-hop. 'Fight the Power', a protest record about censorship on the radio, gave Public Enemy's own 1989 song both its name and, according to sample-credit databases, part of its rhythm track.

signatureTracks.title: It's Your Thing
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Their self-released breakthrough on their own T-Neck label, and a widely sampled funk foundation.

signatureTracks.title: Fight the Power (Part 1)
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Its title and part of its rhythm track were sampled directly on Public Enemy's song of the same name.
